Knapsack Family: 0/1, Unbounded, and the Loop Order That Decides Everything

A large share of interview DP problems are knapsacks in disguise: split an array into two equal halves, put plus and minus signs to hit a target, pay an amount with the fewest coins, count the ways to make change. This page builds the 0/1 table, squeezes it to one row, shows why the capacity loop runs down for 0/1 and up for unbounded, and why swapping the two loops turns "combinations" into "orderings". Every template below was run against tests (Go pending a compiler).
